name: third-mainland
description: GPU-rendered night map of how Lagos moves through a day: 40k particles on real OSM roads, BRT, rail and ferries. three.js WebGPU + WebGL 2 fallback, React, TypeScript, PWA.

paragraphs: A GPU-rendered night map of how Lagos moves through a day. Forty thousand particles flow along the city's real roads, BRT lanes, rail lines and ferry routes, thickening into amber jams on Third Mainland Bridge at 07:40 and thinning out to a trickle at midnight. Scrub the day, switch to a Saturday or a rain day, and every corridor's speed, journey time and timetable updates with it.
Live: third-mainland.vercel.app · Built by Emmanuel Balogun
Illustrative, not live traffic. The lines are traced from OpenStreetMap; the flows on them come from a hand-tuned model of a Lagos day. The app says so on screen, too.
features: Scrub the day. Drag the demand histogram, use the arrow keys, or jump to the morning peak, midday,
Change the kind of day. Weekday, Saturday (midday market peak, thinner timetables) or a rain day
Filter by mode. The legend is also the layer switch: road, BRT, ferry and rail.
Sort by slowest, busiest or A–Z, with a speed sparkline for the selected corridor.
Pan, pinch, scroll and zoom, by mouse, touch or keyboard. Station and terminal names show as you zoom in.
